nodes.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $d_1, \dots, d_r$, $a_1, \dots, a_r$ and $k$ be integers, and put $a_i' = -a_i + (d_i - 1)k$. Then the map $x \mapsto -(x + k)$ is a digraph isomorphism from $G(d_1 n + a_1, \dots, d_r n + a_r)$ onto $G(d_1 n + a_1', \dots, d_r n + a_r')$.
nodes.title: Reflection isomorphism of exact covering system digraphs

nodes.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$, let $d_1, \dots, d_r$, $a_1, \dots, a_r$ and $k$ be integers, and put $a_i' = a_i - (d_i - 1)k$. Then the map $x \mapsto x + k$ is a digraph isomorphism from $G(d_1 n + a_1, \dots, d_r n + a_r)$ onto $G(d_1 n + a_1', \dots, d_r n + a_r')$.
nodes.title: Translation isomorphism of exact covering system digraphs

nodes.summary: For all integers $d_1, d_2, a_1, a_2, x, y$, the digraph $G(d_1 n + a_1, d_2 n + a_2)$ has an edge $x \to y$ iff $y = d_1 x + a_1$ or $y = d_2 x + a_2$.
nodes.title: Out-neighbours in a two-rule digraph

nodes.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $d_1, \dots, d_r$ and $a_1, \dots, a_r$ be integers. The digraph $G(d_1 n + a_1, \dots, d_r n + a_r)$ has vertex set $\mathbb{Z}$ and an edge $x \to y$ iff $y = d_i x + a_i$ for some $i \in \{1, \dots, r\}$.
nodes.title: Edge relation of an exact covering system digraph

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $D$ be an integer with $|D| = d$, and let $a_1, \dots, a_d$ be integers such that for every integer $n$ there is exactly one $i$ with $D \mid n - a_i$. Let $G = G(Dn + a_1, \dots, Dn + a_d)$. Then every integer $z$ can be written as $z = \sum_{j=0}^{k} b_j D^j$ with $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and digits $b_0, \dots, b_k \in \{a_1, \dots, a_d\}$ if and only if the underlying undirected…
nodes.title: Digit representations and connected digraphs

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2$ be integers with $a_1 - a_2$ odd. Then every residue class modulo $|a_1 - a_2|$ contains a vertex that lies on a directed cycle of $G(-2n + a_1, -2n + a_2)$.
nodes.title: Cyclic vertices in every residue class

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2, x, y$ be integers and $k \in \mathbb{N}$. If $y$ is a $k$-descendant of $x$ in $G(-2n + a_1, -2n + a_2)$, that is, the end of a directed walk of exactly $k$ edges from $x$, then
nodes.title: Descendants modulo the difference of offsets

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an odd natural number and $G = G(-2n, -2n + a)$. A cycle of $G$ is a list $(c_1, \dots, c_t)$, $t \ge 1$, of distinct integers with edges $c_1 \to c_2, \dots, c_{t-1} \to c_t$ and $c_t \to c_1$; a vertex is cyclic if it lies on a cycle. For an integer $x$ let $\hat{x}$ be the representative of $x$ modulo $a$ in the interval $(-a/3, 2a/3]$, and let $\operatorname{ord}_q(-2)$ be the multiplicative order of…
nodes.title: Cycles of $G(-2n, -2n + a)$

nodes.summary: For an even integer $a$, the underlying undirected graph of $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ is connected iff $a = 1 + 3^m$ or $a = 1 - 3^m$ for some integer $m \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Connectivity of $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$

nodes.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ be an integer and $a = 1 + 3^m$ or $a = 1 - 3^m$. Then in $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ the least $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $a - 1$ is a $k$-descendant of $0$ (the end of a directed walk of exactly $k$ edges from $0$) is $3^m$, and the least $k$ such that $-(a - 1)$ is a $k$-descendant of $0$ is also $3^m$.
nodes.title: Shortest walks to $\pm(a - 1)$ in $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$

nodes.summary: Let $d_1, d_2 \in \{2, -2\}$ and let $a_1, a_2$ be integers with $a_1 - a_2$ odd. If the exact covering system digraph $G(d_1 n + a_1, d_2 n + a_2)$, with an edge $m \to d_i m + a_i$ for every integer $m$ and $i = 1, 2$, has a single component, that is, any two integers are joined by a path in its underlying undirected graph, then it is isomorphic as a digraph to $G(2n, -2n + 1)$ or to $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ for…
nodes.title: Single-component degree-2 ECSDs up to isomorphism

nodes.summary: Let $d_1, d_2 \in \{2, -2\}$ and let $a_1, a_2$ be integers with $a_1 - a_2$ odd, excluding the case $d_1 = d_2 = -2$ with $|a_1 - a_2| = 1$. Consider the exact covering system digraph $G(d_1 n + a_1, d_2 n + a_2)$, with an edge $m \to d_i m + a_i$ for every integer $m$ and $i = 1, 2$. It has a single component (any two integers are joined by a path in its underlying undirected graph) and a directed walk of…
nodes.title: Degree-2 ECSDs with one component and $0$ on a cycle

nodes.summary: For an integer $b$ write $G_b$ for the digraph $G(2n, -2n + b)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$, with an edge $m \to 2m$ and an edge $m \to -2m + b$ for every integer $m$. Let $a$ be an odd natural number. Then (i) $G_a$ has a loop at $m$ if and only if $m = 0$ or $3m = a$; (ii) $G_a$ has a directed walk of positive length from $m$ back to $m$ if and only if $0 \le m < a/2$; (iii) for all natural numbers $t$ and $a'$ with…
nodes.title: Cycles of the digraph $G(2n, -2n + a)$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ and $m$ be integers and let $k \ge 1$. In the digraph $G(2n, -2n + a)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$, with an edge $x \to 2x$ and an edge $x \to -2x + a$ for every integer $x$, the $k$-descendants of $m$ (the ends of directed walks of exactly $k$ edges from $m$) are exactly the integers $2^k m$, the integers $2^k m - ba$ and $-(2^k m - ba)$ for natural numbers $b$ with $1 \le b < 2^{k-1}$, and $-(2^k m - 2^{k-1} a)$.
nodes.title: Descendants in the digraph $G(2n, -2n + a)$

nodes.summary: For an integer $b$ write $G_b$ for the digraph $G(2n, 2n - b)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$, with an edge $m \to 2m$ and an edge $m \to 2m - b$ for every integer $m$. Let $a$ be an odd natural number, write $x \bmod a$ for the residue of $x$ in $\{0, \dots, a - 1\}$, and write $\operatorname{ord}(2, q)$ for the multiplicative order of $2$ modulo $q$. Then (i) $G_a$ has a loop at $m$ if and only if $m = 0$ or $m = a$; (ii) $G_a$…
nodes.title: Cycles of the digraph $G(2n, 2n - a)$

nodes.summary: For all integers $a_1, a_2$ with $a_1 - a_2$ odd, the exact covering system digraph $G(2n + a_1, 2n + a_2)$, with an edge $m \to 2m + a_1$ and an edge $m \to 2m + a_2$ for every integer $m$, is isomorphic as a digraph to $G(2n, 2n - a)$ for some odd natural number $a$.
nodes.title: Normal form of the ECSDs $G(2n + a_1, 2n + a_2)$

nodes.summary: For all integers $a_1, a_2$ with $a_1 - a_2$ odd, the exact covering system digraph $G(-2n + a_1, -2n + a_2)$, with an edge $m \to -2m + a_1$ and an edge $m \to -2m + a_2$ for every integer $m$, is isomorphic as a digraph to one of the following: $G(-2n, -2n + a)$ for an odd natural number $a$ (Type 3.1); $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ for an even natural number $a$ with $a \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ (Type 3.2); or…
nodes.title: Normal forms of the ECSDs $G(-2n + a_1, -2n + a_2)$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an even integer with $a \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, and let $m$ be an integer such that the digraph $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$, with an edge $x \to -2x + 1$ and an edge $x \to -2x + a$ for every integer $x$, has a directed walk of positive length from $m$ back to $m$. If $a \ge 2$, then $-(a - 1)/3 < m < 2a/3$; if $a \le -2$, then $-2(|a| + 1)/3 < m < (|a| + 3)/3$.
nodes.title: Bounds on the cyclic vertices of $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ when $a \equiv 2 \pmod 3$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an even integer with $a \equiv 2 \pmod 3$, and call an integer $m$ cyclic if the digraph $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$, with an edge $x \to -2x + 1$ and an edge $x \to -2x + a$ for every integer $x$, has a directed walk of positive length from $m$ back to $m$. Then: if $a \ge 2$, every integer $m$ with $-(a - 1)/3 < m < 2a/3$ is cyclic; if $a \le -2$, every integer $m$ with…
nodes.title: Cyclic vertices of $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ and their residues when $a \equiv 2 \pmod 3$

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an even natural number with $a \equiv 1 \pmod 3$ and let $m$ be an integer. The digraph $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ on $\mathbb{Z}$, with an edge $x \to -2x + 1$ and an edge $x \to -2x + a$ for every integer $x$, has a directed walk of positive length from $m$ back to $m$ if and only if $-(a - 1)/3 < m < 2a/3$.
nodes.title: Cyclic vertices of $G(-2n + 1, -2n + a)$ when $a \equiv 1 \pmod 3$

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2 \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $a_1 - a_2$ odd, and write $G(2n + a_1, -2n + a_2)$ for the exact covering system digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ with an edge $m \to n$ exactly when $n = 2m + a_1$ or $n = -2m + a_2$. Then there is an odd natural number $a$ such that $G(2n + a_1, -2n + a_2)$ is isomorphic as a digraph to $G(2n, -2n + a)$, the digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ with an edge $m \to n$ exactly when $n = 2m$ or…
nodes.title: Normal form of Type 2 exact covering system digraphs

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ and let $x, y \in \mathbb{Z}$. The list $(x, y)$ is a cycle of $R$ if and only if $x \ne y$ and $R$ has both edges $x \to y$ and $y \to x$.
nodes.title: Two-vertex cycles of a digraph on the integers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ and let $x \in \mathbb{Z}$. The one-element list $(x)$ is a cycle of $R$ if and only if $R$ has a loop $x \to x$.
nodes.title: One-vertex cycles of a digraph on the integers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$, given by its edge relation. A list $c = (c_1, \dots, c_t)$ of integers is a cycle of $R$ when it is nonempty, its entries are pairwise distinct, and $R$ has the edges $c_1 \to c_2, \dots, c_{t-1} \to c_t$ and $c_t \to c_1$ (for $t = 1$ this means a loop $c_1 \to c_1$).
nodes.title: Cycles of a digraph on the integers

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ and let $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then $n$ is a $1$-descendant of $m$ in $R$ if and only if $R$ has an edge $m \to n$.
nodes.title: The $1$-descendants are the out-neighbours

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$ and let $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then $n$ is a $0$-descendant of $m$ in $R$ if and only if $n = m$.
nodes.title: The only $0$-descendant of a vertex is itself

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a digraph on $\mathbb{Z}$, let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $m, n \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then $n$ is a $k$-descendant of $m$ in $R$ when there is a directed walk of exactly $k$ edges from $m$ to $n$, that is, integers $m = x_0, x_1, \dots, x_k = n$ such that $R$ has an edge $x_{i-1} \to x_i$ for every $1 \le i \le k$.
nodes.title: $k$-descendants in a digraph on the integers

nodes.summary: Let $a \in \mathbb{Z}$. Every integer $z$ can be written as $z = \sum_{j=0}^{k} b_j (-2)^j$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and digits $b_0, \dots, b_k \in \{1, a\}$ if and only if $a = 1 + 3^m$ or $a = 1 - 3^m$ for some integer $m \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Negabinary representations with digits $1$ and $a$

nodes.summary: Let $a_1, a_2 \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $|a_1 - a_2| \ne 1$. Every integer $z$ can be written as $z = \sum_{j=0}^{k} b_j (-2)^j$ for some $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and digits $b_0, \dots, b_k \in \{a_1, a_2\}$ if and only if $|a_1 - a_2| = 3^m$ for some integer $m \ge 0$, neither $a_1$ nor $a_2$ is divisible by $3$, and $\max\{|a_1|, |a_2|\} \le 2|a_1 - a_2| - 1$.
nodes.title: Negabinary representations with two digits

nodes.summary: Let $n > 3$ be a natural number. If $3n$ divides $2^n + 1$, then $9$ divides $n$.
nodes.title: Nine divides $n$ when $n > 3$ and $3n$ divides $2^n + 1$

nodes.summary: For every integer $n$ and every natural number $k$, if $3n$ divides $1 - (-2)^k$, then $9n$ divides $1 - (-2)^{3k}$.
nodes.title: Divisibility of $1 - (-2)^{3k}$ from $1 - (-2)^k$

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$, if $3n$ divides $2^n + 1$, then $9n$ divides $2^{3n} + 1$.
nodes.title: Divisibility of $2^{3n} + 1$ from $2^n + 1$

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $m$ and $k$, if $3^{m+1}$ does not divide $2^k + 1$, then $3^{m+2}$ does not divide $2^{3k} + 1$.
nodes.title: Bounding the power of $3$ dividing $2^{3k} + 1$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
